title: The auditory nerve carries the ear's signal into the brain
summary: The auditory nerve carries the cochlea's electrical signal to the brain, which turns it into a sound a person recognizes.
body: NIDCD says the auditory nerve carries the electrical signal to the brain. The brain turns it into a sound that we recognize and understand. That is the last step on the institute's how-we-hear page. Recognition here is the page's wording for that arrival, not a theory of attention.

sources.title: How Do We Hear?
sources.author: NIDCD
sources.note: Supports the auditory nerve carrying the electrical signal to the brain, which turns it into a recognized sound.
